statement: Two trees that have identical degree sequences are isomorphic to each other.
definitions: Tree = finite, connected, acyclic simple graph. Degree sequence = the multiset (non-increasing list) of vertex degrees. Isomorphic = there is an edge-preserving bijection of vertex sets.
ground_truth_witness: T1 on {0,...,5} with edges {0-1, 1-2, 2-3, 3-4, 2-5} and T2 on {0,...,5} with edges {0-1, 1-2, 2-3, 3-4, 1-5}. Both are trees (connected with 5 edges) and both have sorted degree sequence (3,2,2,1,1,1); but in T1 the branches hanging off the degree-3 vertex have sizes (2,2,1) while in T2 they have sizes (3,1,1), and checking all 720 vertex bijections confirms that no isomorphism exists.
reference_authority: published counterexample (book-cited), verified per partB_feasibility records
book_citation: M. Capobianco and J. C. Molluzzo, Examples and Counterexamples in Graph Theory, North-Holland, New York, 1978, ISBN 0-444-00255-3 (xii+259 pp.). Cited generally: the specific example number could not be identified from freely available tables of contents or secondary discussions.

skeptic.objection: Precise and false. Verified: both edge sets are trees on 6 vertices, both have degree sequence (3,2,2,1,1,1), and none of the 720 bijections is an isomorphism (in T1 the degree-3 vertex is adjacent to both degree-2 vertices, in T2 to only one). Thematically adjacent to roster cb-mse-r01-degree-sequence-isomorphism, but that item's witness (C7 vs C4+C3) does not refute the tree claim and the claims differ, so not a duplicate under the same-claim/same-witness rule. Easy (difficulty 1) but a genuine small construction, not name-dropping. Book citation is only generic (example number not identified), which is acceptable since verification is computational.

bank_overlap.rationale: No entry refutes 'trees with equal degree sequences are isomorphic' (grep 'same degree sequence' empty). se-math-2469696-q concerns tree degree sequences but refutes a different inference (degree-sum equality does not force the pointwise degree sequence); other degree-sequence entries use degree sequences merely to certify non-isomorphism.
